description:
From the op-ffg6 audit, 2026-08-13. Everything else in the unwrap programme depends on this. Non-API-breaking. ~1 day.

Scope: src/lib/tuas_lib_error/mod.rs ONLY (note: it is mod.rs, not tuas_lib_error.rs).

1. ADD PAYLOAD to ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError -- material, requested temperature, and the violated bound.
   It is currently a UNIT variant, which is exactly why the htgr_sim_v1 crash reported no material, no node and no
   temperature. Constructed in ~40 places, all as a bare unit value, so this is mechanical and non-breaking to callers
   that only match on the variant.
2. ADD MISSING VARIANTS the audit found no home for:
   - RootFindingFailure (Brent / regula falsi / bisect non-convergence)
   - PoisonedLock (not represented at all today)
   - CorrelationRangeError -- input outside a CORRELATION's validated envelope, distinct from a property-table range.
     95 panic! in nusselt_number_correlations/pipe_correlations.rs are this ('gnielinski Re > 1e6, too high').
   - NonPhysicalInput (viscosity <= 0, density <= 0, hydraulic diameter <= 0)
   - EmptyCollection (general case; CourantMassFlowVectorEmpty is hyper-specific)
   - SingularMatrix{col} -- MatrixError::Singular{col} already exists at src/lib/matrix.rs:39 but its single call site
     (standalone_fluid_nodes/mod.rs:56) flattens it into GenericStringError and loses the column index.
3. COORDINATE NAMING WITH op-t647 before freezing. That bead is building a bounds-checked Result facade in
   tampines-steam-tables. htgr_sim_v1's steam_generator.rs imports BOTH crates, so it should handle ONE shape of
   'input outside validated envelope' error, not two. The audit recommends sharing the error vocabulary while NOT
   copying the facade structure.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
PARTIALLY DONE by the main session, 2026-08-13, at the maintainer's direction ('let's deal with the ThermophysicalPropertyRangeError, add those fields and match arms'). NOT yet compiled -- cargo is being held off while an agent owns the build lock on the digital-twin-engine crate.

DONE:
1. ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError is now a STRUCT variant carrying { material: String, temperature,
   lower_bound, upper_bound } -- the last three uom ThermodynamicTemperature. Display renders in BOTH kelvin and degC,
   because the property tables are in kelvin and plant data is quoted in Celsius.
   LAYERING NOTE: material is a String, not a Material. tuas_lib_error is Layer 0 and boussinesq_thermophysical_properties
   is Layer 1, so holding the real type would invert the crate's module layering. Documented on the variant.
2. Added TuasLibError::temperature_out_of_range(material: impl Debug, temperature, lower, upper) so call sites do not
   hand-build a 4-field struct literal whose three same-typed temperatures are easy to transpose. Has a doctest.
3. Added CorrelationRangeError { parameter, value, lower_bound, upper_bound, units } -- NOT in the original plan, added
   because nuclear_graphite.rs was reporting a FLUENCE bound violation as a TEMPERATURE range error. Keeping the old
   variant there would have meant inventing a temperature. f64 rather than uom deliberately: the variant is generic over
   quantity kinds so the unit cannot live in the type, hence the explicit  field.
4. Updated all 10 sites the compiler flagged: mod.rs range_check (x2), custom_liquid_material (x2 -> merged into one),
   custom_solid_material (x2 -> merged into one), nuclear_graphite (now CorrelationRangeError), thermal_conductivity.rs
   match pattern, and 3 test match patterns in ss_304_l_high_temp.rs. Plus the Into<String> arm.
5. REMOVED the println!/dbg! pairs in the three range checkers. They existed only because the error carried no payload,
   and they printed on EVERY failing call -- in a per-node-per-timestep property loop that is thousands of identical
   lines to stdout while the returned error still said nothing. The detail now travels with the error.
6. Converted thermal_conductivity.rs's Err(_) => todo!() to return the error. Nothing there was unimplemented; the
   SteelSS304L spline fallback simply does not apply to non-range errors.

STILL TO DO on this bead: RootFindingFailure, PoisonedLock, EmptyCollection, NonPhysicalInput, SingularMatrix{col}.
And coordinate the CorrelationRangeError naming with op-t647 before that bead freezes its own vocabulary.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
VERIFIED, 2026-08-13. cargo check -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib --tests: exit 0, no errors.

Tests run in release mode, all passing:
  - 31/31 boussinesq_thermophysical_properties lib tests (no regression from the payload change)
  - 1/1 doctest on TuasLibError::temperature_out_of_range
  - 2/2 NEW tests in tuas_lib_error::tests, added for this change:
      temperature_range_error_names_material_temperature_and_both_bounds
      correlation_range_error_does_not_claim_a_temperature_failed
    Both carry methodology + measured results + date in their doc comments per the V&V rule.

ACTUAL RENDERED OUTPUT (observed, not predicted):
  thermophysical property temperature out of range: "SteelSS304L" was evaluated at 1100.00 K (826.85 degC),
  outside its tabulated range 250.00 K to 1000.00 K (-23.15 degC to 726.85 degC)

  fluence gam = 17 is outside the correlation's validated range [0, 15] (10^25 n/m^2, E > 0.1 MeV)

Compare the OLD message for the first case, which was the fixed text 'Temperature supplied for
thermophysical_properties function was out of range' -- no material, no temperature, no bound. That is why the
htgr_sim_v1 crash was undiagnosable from its output.

Note the quotes around SteelSS304L: the test passes a &str and the payload is built with Debug, which quotes string
slices. A real caller passing a Material renders unquoted as Solid(SteelSS304L). Recorded in the test doc so the
documented output matches what the test actually prints.

Two message-format corrections made after first observing the output: the CorrelationRangeError format printed its
units TWICE (once after the value, once after the bounds); now printed once in parentheses at the end. And the V&V doc
comment initially recorded the temperature message WITHOUT the quotes, which did not match reality -- corrected.
